what: Clementina Arena's 1921 crossing — WITHDRAWN. IT IS SOMEBODY ELSE'S.
result: US/PASS/NY/ELLIS2/000191616/3 is a different Clementina Arena.
note: THIS ARCHIVE RECORDED A CROSSING IT HAD NOT CHECKED. The identification rested on a NAME AND A YEAR and nothing else: a Clementina Arena arriving at New York in 1921, and a Clementina Arena born in Manhattan in December 1900. THE TRANSCRIPTS OF THE NEIGHBOURING LINES DESTROY IT. The same manifest -- ship GIUSEPPE VERDI out of NAPLES -- carries at line 1 ROSA ARENA, aged 27, born 1894, whose RESIDENCE IS GIVEN AS VITTORIA, in the province of RAGUSA in SICILY, and whose FATHER is named at line 2 as GIOVANNI. Line 3, Clementina, is entered as ROSA'S SISTER. SO THE CLEMENTINA ARENA OF THIS MANIFEST IS A SICILIAN WOMAN FROM VITTORIA, daughter of a Giovanni Arena, travelling with her sister. She is not the Manhattan-born daughter of Rocco Arena and Generosa Costa. AND THAT MAKES A SECOND CORRECTION NECESSARY. On the morning of 14 September this archive 'corrected' The Crossings, which had said Clementina's 1921 crossing was NOT FOUND, on the strength of this very record. THE ORIGINAL STATEMENT WAS RIGHT. Clementina Arena's 1921 crossing is NOT FOUND, and the archive has now been wrong about it in both directions in a single day -- first by trusting an inherited identification, then by trusting it again to overturn a true negative.

what: The signed-out session, resolved — and why a lapsed subscription is not a negative
result: Access restored 16 September 2026 when the account holder took a full month's subscription and signed in. Everything this row listed as wanted has now been run.
note: KEPT BECAUSE OF WHAT IT NEARLY DID TO THE RECORD. For three days this archive carried a row whose result field read like a finding and was actually a closed door: the trial had lapsed mid-search. A LAPSED SUBSCRIPTION, A PAYWALL AND A SIGNED-OUT SESSION ARE ALL THE SAME THING -- the absence of an answer, not an answer -- and all three were sitting in a file whose other rows are evidence. The convention this produced is now general: A LOCK IS RECORDED AS A LOCK, IT IS OWNED BY WHOEVER CAN OPEN IT, AND IT IS RE-RUN THE MOMENT THEY DO. what: Rocco Arlotta — THE 1900 LODGER, IDENTIFIED
result: Married ANTONIETTA TAVANI, 4 June 1900, Manhattan. Aged 22, born 1878. Father ANTONIO ARLOTTA, mother NICOLINA CARATOZZOLA.
note: The Arlotta lodging with Rocco Arena in the 1900 census -- 'Rocco Arlotta, 23' -- was one of the five circumstantial supports for this archive's correction of the Arena parentage, and until now he was only an age and a surname. FindMyPast's United States Marriages index gives him whole: ROCCO ARLOTTA, 22, born 1878, married ANTONIETTA TAVANI, 19, on 4 JUNE 1900 IN MANHATTAN -- the same month the census enumerated him under Rocco Arena's roof. His father was ANTONIO ARLOTTA and his mother NICOLINA CARATOZZOLA; hers Giovanni Tavani and Peppina Fusto. THIS ALSO CLOSES A NEAR MISS. This archive had two candidate arrivals from the Statue of Liberty index -- 16 May 1898 aged 32 and 5 May 1904 -- and neither fitted the census age. The 1898 man, born about 1866, is somebody else. The lodger is the man born 1878. AND HE STAYED. The New York Roman Catholic parish index has a Rocco Arlotta baptising children at OUR LADY OF LORETTO in 1905 and 1908 -- the same Manhattan parish where Rocco Arena's daughters Serafina and Clementina were baptised. He is not a stranger boarding with strangers; he is part of the same Scilla colony in the same few streets. NOTE: his father is ANTONIO, not the GIOVANNI ARLOTTA who is Serafina's father, so he is not her nephew. A cousin is likelier, and untested.

what: Our Lady of Loretto — the Scilla colony in one Manhattan parish
result: Eighty-four Arena baptisms in the New York Roman Catholic parish index, with the father's given name against each.
note: The index rows are readable even where the transcripts are not, and they show a community rather than a family. At OUR LADY OF LORETTO alone the Arena fathers are ROCCO, GIOVANNI, ROSARIO, MICHELE, FELICE, PIETRO, MARIANO, IGNAZIO, ANGELO, VINCENZO, GIACOMO and AURELIO. THREE OF ROCCO ARENA'S OWN CHILDREN ARE THERE: Antonio, born 1896; Serafina, born 1898; Clementina, born 1900 and baptised 1901. AND TWO THAT MAY BE HIS BROTHER'S. An ANGELICA ARENA, born and baptised 1900, father entered as GIOVANNIE; and a MICHELA ARENA, born 1908, father GIOVANNI. Giovanni Arena, Rocco's brother, landed in May 1899 and was lodging with Rocco in June 1900. If either child is his, he did not go straight home -- and the family tree has neither. RECORDED AS A LEAD: the index gives no mother, and there are several Giovanni Arena in the same parish register.

what: RETRACTED — the godparents are not behind that paywall, because they are not in the record at all
result: The full transcript has now been read. ITS FIELDS ARE: record set, name, birth year, baptism year, parish, county, state, country, MOTHER'S first and last name, FATHER'S first and last name, birth date, baptism date, location, archdiocese, RESIDENCE, language. THERE IS NO GODPARENT FIELD, and there is no «View original record» button -- these baptisms are TRANSCRIPT ONLY, with no image.
note: THIS ROW SAID THE TRANSCRIPT CARRIED «THE MOTHER'S NAME AND THE GODPARENTS» AND CALLED IT THE SINGLE RICHEST UNOPENED SEAM FOR THE AMERICAN YEARS. HALF OF THAT WAS TRUE. The mother's name is there and it has been worth everything -- it attached four children to Rocco Arena and excluded two strangers. THE GODPARENTS WERE NEVER THERE. The claim was made while the record was locked, by reasoning from what a parish baptism register contains rather than from what this index transcribes, and A GUESS ABOUT THE CONTENTS OF A LOCKED RECORD IS NOT A FINDING. WORSE, THERE IS NO ROUTE TO THEM HERE: with no image, the godparents cannot be reached at any subscription tier. They exist only in the original Our Lady of Loretto register, which means the Archdiocese of New York's own archive. THE REASONING THAT FAILED IS WORTH KEEPING: godparents in an Italian parish usually are kin, and that remains true -- it is just not something this source can tell us.

what: Rosa Arena and Clementina Arena of Vittoria — a different family
result: Giuseppe Verdi out of Naples, 1921. Rosa 27, b.1894, resident VITTORIA (Ragusa), father GIOVANNI; Clementina entered as her sister.
note: Recorded so that nobody identifies them with this family again. VITTORIA is in the province of RAGUSA, at the other end of Sicily from Piedimonte Etneo and four hundred kilometres from Scilla. The Arena of that manifest have no connection to this archive beyond the surname -- which, as the Our Lady of Loretto index shows, was carried by at least twelve unrelated households in New York alone.

what: Rocco Arena's four crossings — all four now named, dated and with a ship
result: 1892 ELYSIA ex Naples, aged 31; 1894 SUEVIA ex Naples, aged 33; 1900 TRAVE ex Genoa, aged 39; 1913 SAN GUGLIELMO ex Messina, aged 52. Indexed birth year 1861 on every one.
note: The archive had these four as a list with one ship and one 'probable'. FindMyPast's passenger index gives all four with the vessel, the port and a consistent birth year of 1861 -- FOUR independent clerks over twenty-one years agreeing with the birth act of 20 December 1861. AND THE 1894 CROSSING IS NO LONGER PROBABLE. It is indexed at age THIRTY-THREE with the same birth year, on the SUEVIA out of Naples. THE 1900 RECORD SAYS SOMETHING THE ARCHIVE DID NOT KNOW: nationality US CITIZEN, residence SCILLA. He had already naturalised by March 1900 and was living at Scilla while holding American citizenship -- which is why the 1900 census, taken three months later, finds him in Manhattan with a wife and two children and calls him a citizen.

what: The 1913 crossing names his wife and a nephew
result: San Guglielmo out of Messina, 1913. Rocco Arena, 52, US Citizen. DEPARTURE PORT RELATION (WIFE): CORTA GENEROSA. ARRIVAL PORT RELATION (NEPHEW): ANTONIO ARENA.
note: THE RICHEST LINE IN THE WHOLE PASSENGER HARVEST, and it comes from a field this archive had never read: the manifest's RELATION columns, which name who a passenger left behind and who they were going to. LEFT BEHIND AT MESSINA: his wife, entered as CORTA GENEROSA -- Generosa Costa, with the surname mangled. So in 1913 Rocco sailed for New York and Generosa did not. GOING TO, IN NEW YORK: a NEPHEW called ANTONIO ARENA. Rocco's own son Antonio was born in Manhattan in 1896 and would be seventeen; a clerk could have written nephew for son, but the index is explicit. If it is right, it is a son of GIOVANNI or GIUSEPPE ARENA -- Rocco's brothers -- already established in New York by 1913, and the family tree has no such person. RECORDED AS A LEAD.

what: Anna Arena's 1899 crossing — a second index agrees

FindMyPast indexes the same line independently and adds the residence: SCILLA. what: The other Giovanni Arena of 1899 is from Serra San Bruno

what: Giuseppe Arena of Scilla — no American crossing indexed
result: Zero results for Giuseppe Arena with Scilla in the travel and migration records.
note: Rocco's brother Giuseppe married Maria Martello in 1885 and was still at Scilla in 1898, when his ten-month-old son died at Via Acquagrande 30. There is no indexed crossing for him. Of the three brothers, GIOVANNI and ROCCO went to America and GIUSEPPE appears to have stayed.

what: Rocco Arlotta's children name his parents back — three for three
result: Our Lady of Loretto: NICOLINA b.1901, ANTONIO b.1903, PAPPINA (Peppina) b.1904, father ROCCO in each.
note: The strongest confirmation in the whole American harvest, and it comes from three free index rows. Rocco Arlotta's marriage act of June 1900 gives his father as ANTONIO ARLOTTA, his mother as NICOLINA CARATOZZOLA, and his wife's mother as PEPPINA FUSTO. His children, baptised at the Arena's own parish, are NICOLINA (1901), ANTONIO (1903) and PEPPINA (1904). FIRST DAUGHTER FOR THE PATERNAL GRANDMOTHER, FIRST SON FOR THE PATERNAL GRANDFATHER, SECOND DAUGHTER FOR THE MATERNAL GRANDMOTHER. Textbook southern Italian naming custom, three for three, and it proves that the man who lodged with Rocco Arena in 1900, the man who married Antonietta Tavani that June, and the man baptising children at Our Lady of Loretto are ONE MAN. TWO OTHER ARLOTTA HOUSEHOLDS ARE IN THE SAME REGISTER: a FRANCESCO Arlotta with six children between 1901 and 1911, and a GIOVANNI Arlotta with a Maria Carmela in 1896. The Arlotta were in New York in numbers, like the Arena.

what: Rocco Arena has no naturalisation petition in this collection
result: Zero matching records; the Rocco Arena entries are born 1896 and petition in 1942-44.
note: He is entered as a US CITIZEN on the manifests of BOTH March 1900 and 1913, so his declaration and petition exist -- but not here. The United States Naturalization Petitions set on FindMyPast begins too late for him. His papers are in an earlier New York court series, and finding them means the National Archives at New York City rather than a subscription site.

what: Antonio Arena, born New York 1896, is not in the New York draft cards
result: The New York WWI registrations hold an Antonio Arena born 1876 and an «Antonio Rena» Arena born 1886. Neither is 1896.
note: Rocco's eldest son was born in Manhattan on 4 October 1896 and was therefore an American citizen who should have registered in 1917-18. HE DID NOT, in New York. That is evidence, not just an absence: taken with Rocco's missing 1910 census entry and the 1913 manifest on which he sails WITHOUT Generosa, it says the family had gone back to Italy and the children with them. The boy born in Manhattan was living at Scilla when his own country called him up.

what: ANTONIO ARENA'S BAPTISM — and the Mulberry Street address, confirmed
result: Born 3 OCTOBER 1896, baptised 15 NOVEMBER 1896 at OUR LADY OF LORETTO, Manhattan. Father ROCCO ARENA, mother GENEROSA COSTA. RESIDENCE: 141 MULBERRY STREET.
note: THE PAYWALL IS OPEN AND THE FIRST TRANSCRIPT SETTLED SOMETHING. This archive knew an Antonio Arena born in New York in 1896 existed -- the WWI registration row below records looking for him -- but had no act. Now it has one, and the act names BOTH PARENTS: Rocco Arena and Generosa Costa, married at Scilla in December 1888. THE ADDRESS IS THE SECOND FINDING. «141 Mulberry» is the first street address this archive has ever had for the New York household -- and it CORROBORATES THE ELLIS ISLAND MANIFEST OF 1899, where Giovanni Arena sails to join «BROTHER ROCCO, N. YORK, MULBERRY ST». Two independent documents, one street. AND IT DATES THE EMIGRATION FROM THE INSIDE: Rocco married at Scilla in December 1888, his daughter Anna was born at Scilla in January 1893, and his son Antonio was born in Manhattan in October 1896. The household crossed between those two dates -- which fits the 1892 and 1894 crossings already documented.

what: THE WHOLE NEW YORK HOUSEHOLD — four children, two addresses, one infant death
result: Antonio b. 3 Oct 1896 (141 Mulberry); Serafina b. 15 Aug 1898 (141 Mulberry); Clementina b. 21 Dec 1900 (198 Mulberry); Antonio b. 13 Oct 1902 (Most Precious Blood). All «father Rocco Arena, mother Generosa Costa».
note: FIVE ARENA BAPTISMS IN ALL OF NEW YORK NAME A FATHER ROCCO, AND FOUR OF THEM ARE OURS. The fifth -- GIUSEPPE, 1911, Our Lady of Mount Carmel in the Bronx -- gives the mother as TERESA SINISCALDI and is a different Rocco Arena entirely. Checking the mother is what separated them, and a surname sweep alone would have taken all five. TWO SONS NAMED ANTONIO, six years apart, means the first died: the same reading this archive made of Orazio Arena's two sons named Domenico at Scilla. THE ADDRESSES ARE NEW AND THEY CORROBORATE AN OLD RECORD: 141 MULBERRY in 1896 and 1898, 198 MULBERRY by 1901. The Ellis Island manifest of 1899 sends Giovanni Arena to «BROTHER ROCCO, N. YORK, MULBERRY ST» -- two independent sources, one street, and now a number.

what: Joannem Arena, married at Our Lady of Loretto in 1899, is a Palermo family and not ours
result: Groom's father THOMAE ARENA, mother ANGELICAE COGLITORE, residence PALERMO; bride IGNATIAM ARNATO of POLIZZI GENEROSA, daughter of Vincentii Arnato and Losephae Fiorito. Married 17 December 1899.
note: THE TIMING WAS THE TRAP AND THE MOTHER'S NAME SPRANG IT. Rocco Arena's brother GIOVANNI landed at New York in May 1899 to join «BROTHER ROCCO, N. YORK, MULBERRY ST», and here is a «Joannem Arena» marrying at the Arena family's own parish seven months later. It is not him. Our Giovanni Arena was born at Scilla on 30 April 1854 to FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA and SERAFINA ARLOTTA, and he had already married CONCETTA RUSSO at Scilla in 1885, act 86. This groom's parents are Sicilian and so is his bride's town. THIS IS THE SECOND ARENA NAMESAKE THIS COLLECTION HAS OFFERED AND THE SECOND EXCLUDED ON A PARENT'S NAME -- the first was Giuseppe Arena and Teresa Siniscaldi among the baptisms. OUR LADY OF LORETTO SERVED SICILIANS AS WELL AS CALABRIANS, so a surname sweep of that parish will keep returning strangers. Check the parents every time.

what: SEBASTIANO MAZZA ON THE 1959 QUEENSLAND ELECTORAL ROLL — Progress Road, Wacol
result: Sebastiano Mazza, male, BUILDER'S LABOURER, Progress Road, WACOL, sub-district INALA, district McPherson, Queensland, 1959 roll, number 3779. The only Sebastiano Mazza in the entire collection.
note: MICHAEL MAZZA'S GRANDFATHER, IN AN AUSTRALIAN CIVIL RECORD, WITH AN ADDRESS AND A TRADE. Until now this archive held Sebastiano Mazza (1920-2002) in Australia only by his NAA passenger entry and his grave at Nudgee, plot V-1026 -- arrival and death, and nothing in between. This is the in between. WACOL AND INALA ARE THE POINT: that is the post-war migrant housing belt on Brisbane's south-west edge, built for exactly the people who arrived on the 1949 ships, and it is where he is living ten years after landing. BUILDER'S LABOURER is the trade of a man who arrived with no English and no capital. It also carries a quieter fact: HE WAS ENROLLED, and enrolment required British subject status, so his NATURALISATION falls between 1949 and 1959 and is a document that exists and has never been looked for.

what: ROSARIO AND ANGELA MAZZA AT 225 LEICHHARDT STREET — one address, and a correction to how it was read
result: ROSARIO MAZZA, SHOPKEEPER, number 1845; ANGELA MAZZA, HOME DUTIES, number 1844. Both at 225 Leichhardt Street, City, Brisbane, 1959 roll.
note: THE ADDRESS IS THE EVIDENCE. THE ROLL NUMBERS ARE NOT, AND THIS ROW FIRST SAID THEY WERE. Both transcripts independently give 225 LEICHHARDT STREET, CITY, BRISBANE, and that co-residence is what puts Rosario and Angela in one house. THE ORIGINAL VERSION OF THIS ROW ARGUED FROM THE NUMBERING -- 1844 and 1845 are consecutive, therefore consecutive lines, therefore one address. THAT REASONING IS WRONG AND THE CRUPI SWEEP THE SAME DAY DISPROVED IT: Antonio Crupi is 504 at DEAN STREET, Francesco Crupi is 505 at INNISFAIL ROAD, Pietro Crupi is 510 at BIRKALA -- consecutive numbers, three different addresses. THE ROLL IS ORDERED ALPHABETICALLY WITHIN A SUB-DISTRICT, not by street, so «Angela» before «Rosario» is nothing more than A before R. The conclusion survives because it never rested on the numbering in the first place; the argument for it did, and the argument was false. WHAT STANDS: Rosario Mazza, SHOPKEEPER, and Angela Mazza, HOME DUTIES, at the same street number in the same year, bearing the names of a couple this archive already holds -- ROSARIO MAZZA (1899-1986), Sebastiano's brother, and his wife ANGELA, born CRUPI and carried by the tree as «Angela Cupo». Neither transcript gives a birth year or a maiden name, so this remains a strong inference and not a proof. WHAT IT MOVES: the archive had this household at TULLY in 1926, where their daughter Carmela was born. By 1959 they are in the middle of Brisbane keeping a shop, while Angela's three brothers are still at Tully.

what: ROSARIO SALVATORE MAZZA, 1949 — 191 Given Terrace, Paddington, shop assistant
result: Rosario Salvatore Mazza, male, SHOP ASSISTANT, 191 Given Terrace, PADDINGTON, Brisbane, Queensland, 1949 roll, number 4788.
note: THE SAME MAN TEN YEARS EARLIER, AND THE MIDDLE NAME IS WHY. Rosario Mazza (b. 1899) is the son of SALVATORE MAZZA (1879-1929), and here he is enrolled as «Rosario Salvatore». There are only two Rosario Mazza in the whole Queensland collection and this is the other one. SHOP ASSISTANT IN 1949, SHOPKEEPER IN 1959: a decade of one man's working life in two words, at two Brisbane addresses -- Paddington, then the city. IT ALSO DATES THE FAMILY'S MOVE SOUTH. Their daughter Carmela was born at TULLY in 1926; by 1949 they are in Brisbane. The move from the north Queensland cane and timber country to the city happened between those two dates.

what: The other Queensland Mazza of 1959 — Tully and Yelarbon, two trades, one of them a lead
result: ANDREA MAZZA, TIMBER CUTTER, Cardwell, sub-district TULLY, district Herbert, number 1422. ANTONIO MAZZA, TOBACCO GROWER, Wyenio, YELARBON, sub-district Inglewood, district Maranoa, number 857.
note: ANDREA MAZZA IS A LEAD AND ANTONIO IS NOT. TULLY IS NOT A COINCIDENCE: Rosario Mazza's daughter CARMELA MAZZA was born at Tully in 1926, so this archive already has a Mazza household in that exact sub-district a generation earlier, and a timber cutter at Cardwell in 1959 is standing where they stood. No Andrea appears anywhere in this family as the tree now has it, which means either he belongs to a branch the tree has not recorded or he is a stranger with the right surname in the right town. IT CANNOT BE SETTLED FROM A ROLL, which carries no parents and no birth year. YELARBON IS FOUR HUNDRED KILOMETRES AWAY on the New South Wales border and tobacco was grown there by Italians with no connection to this family; Antonio is recorded to close him off, not to claim him.

what: DOMENICA PROSTAMO IS NOT ON ANY AUSTRALIAN ELECTORAL ROLL FINDMYPAST HOLDS — under either name
result: «Domenica Mazza» returns ZERO in the collection. «Prostamo» returns ZERO across the whole of Australia, every state and every year.
note: HER HUSBAND IS ON THE 1959 ROLL AND SHE IS NOT, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING. Sebastiano Mazza is enrolled at Wacol in 1959; Domenica Prostamo (1928-2010), his wife, is absent under her married name and her maiden name alike. THE LIKELY READING IS NATURALISATION, NOT ABSENCE. Enrolment required British subject status, and in Italian families of this generation THE HUSBAND WAS ROUTINELY NATURALISED FIRST and the wife years later -- she may simply not have been eligible in 1959. IT IS NOT PROOF OF THAT. The 1959 roll is the LAST Queensland year Findmypast holds, so an enrolment in 1963 or 1968 would be invisible here whatever the cause. THE ABSENCE IS BOUNDED BY THE COLLECTION, NOT BY HER LIFE. ZERO PROSTAMO IN ALL OF AUSTRALIA also means her father Francesco and her brothers are unreachable in this set.

what: What Findmypast's «Australia Electoral Rolls» actually covers for Queensland — eight years, ending 1959
result: QUEENSLAND: commonwealth rolls for 1903, 1906, 1913, 1922, 1934, 1941, 1949 and 1959 only, plus state rolls 1860-1884 and 1895-1915. 45% have images. Other states are thinner still: Western Australia 1939/1943/1949, Tasmania 1916/1934/1943, South Australia 1939/1941/1943, New South Wales 1903/1913/1935.
note: THIS DEFLATES THE INSTRUMENT AND THE WORK LIST SHOULD SAY SO. Rows 49 and 62 promoted electoral rolls as the answer to a family the Queensland BDM indexes cannot see, on the ground that the rolls are NEAR-ANNUAL and would place every household YEAR BY YEAR. That is true of the rolls as they exist. IT IS NOT TRUE OF FINDMYPAST'S HOLDING OF THEM. For a migration that lands in 1949 there are exactly TWO Queensland years in this collection, 1949 and 1959, and the family had barely arrived for the first. ONE USABLE YEAR. The rolls remain the right instrument; Findmypast is not the right holder of them for this family. The full near-annual run is at the National Library of Australia and on Ancestry, and getting past 1959 means one of those.

what: The Findmypast results URL silently corrupts searches when a parameter is wrong — in two different ways
result: VERIFIED PARAMETERS: datasetname, lastname, firstname, and the sort pair o= and d=. UNRECOGNISED ONES DO ONE OF TWO THINGS. «state=Queensland» and «page=2» render a filter chip and report «0 results found». «street=progress road» is discarded in silence and the unfiltered count comes back unchanged.
note: BOTH FAILURES LOOK LIKE ANSWERS AND NEITHER IS. A wrong parameter that ZEROES the count produces a page word for word identical to a genuine negative -- «0 results found» and the same advice to broaden the search -- and this archive writes negatives down as evidence. «state=Queensland» returned zero on a search whose unfiltered form plainly listed Queensland rows, which is the only reason it was caught. A wrong parameter that is IGNORED is the opposite danger: the search you believe you ran is not the search that ran, and the result is real but answers a different question. THE RULE: never record a negative from a parameter that has not been control-tested against a search known to return rows. The earlier «fathersfirstname» for «fatherfirstname» was the ignored kind. PAGINATION HAS NO URL FORM AT ALL -- sort on a column with o= and d= to bring the rows you want onto the first page instead.

what: THE CRUPI OF TULLY — seven of them on one page of the 1959 roll, with trades and addresses
result: Numbers 504-510 in the Tully sub-district: ANTONIO, cane farmer, Dean Street; FRANCESCO, mechanic, Innisfail Road; GIOVANNA, home duties, Feluga; MARIA, home duties, no address; MARIO, lorry driver, no address; NELLIE, home duties, Dean Street; PIETRO, lorry driver, Birkala via Tully.
note: THIS IS ANGELA CRUPI'S FAMILY AND THE ARCHIVE COULD NOT PLACE THEM UNTIL NOW. The Queensland death index gave PIETRO (d. 1961), ANTONINO (d. 1982) and MARIO CRUPI (d. 1989) as her brothers, all three sons of FRANCESCO CRUPI and MARIA VECCHIO; the Brisbane cemetery registers then returned NOTHING for any of them, council and Catholic alike. THE ROLLS FIND THEM ALIVE INSTEAD, AND THEY ARE ALL AT TULLY. Pietro's last enrolment is 1959 and he died in July 1961. ONE COUPLE IS EVIDENCED: Antonio the cane farmer and Nellie both give DEAN STREET TULLY, and a shared address is the thing that pairs them. MARIA AND MARIO ARE NOT EVIDENCED as a couple -- both transcripts leave the address blank, so their adjacency proves nothing. FRANCESCO IS PROBABLY A NEPHEW, NOT THE FATHER: Angela's father Francesco Crupi would have been about eighty-five in 1959 and this one is a working mechanic, so he is far more likely a grandson named for him in the ordinary way. THE BROTHERS STAYED NORTH AND THEIR SISTER CAME SOUTH: Angela is in Brisbane with Rosario Mazza in the same year.

what: The Crupi a decade earlier, and the trades that changed — 1949
result: ANTONIO CRUPI, BOOTMAKER, Bryant Street, Tully. MARIO CRUPI, BUS DRIVER, Mena Creek, sub-district INNISFAIL. A SECOND ANTONIO CRUPI, FARMER, Silkwood East, Innisfail, on the 1959 roll — a different man from the Tully cane farmer.
note: TEN YEARS CHANGES EVERY TRADE IN THIS FAMILY. Antonio is a BOOTMAKER at Bryant Street in 1949 and a CANE FARMER at Dean Street in 1959 -- he left a craft for the land, which is the opposite of the usual migrant direction and worth noticing. Mario is a BUS DRIVER at Mena Creek in the Innisfail sub-district in 1949 and a LORRY DRIVER at Tully in 1959, so he moved south into his brothers' district. THE SECOND ANTONIO IS A WARNING, NOT A FINDING: there are at least two Antonio Crupi in north Queensland in 1959, one farming at Silkwood East in Innisfail and one at Tully, and NOTHING IN A ROLL DISTINGUISHES THEM -- no parents, no birth year. Which one is Angela's brother Antonino, dead in 1982, cannot be settled here.

what: POLISTENA and ROCCO ARENA are on no Australian electoral roll Findmypast holds
result: «Polistena» returns ZERO across the whole of Australia. «Rocco Arena» returns ZERO. The surname Arena returns 172, none of them this family: the Queensland Arena are a Cloncurry family enrolled from 1898 to 1934.
note: THE PATTERN ACROSS FOUR PEOPLE IS THE FINDING, NOT ANY ONE ABSENCE. Of the adults who arrived in 1949, ONLY SEBASTIANO MAZZA is enrolled by 1959. ROCCO ARENA is not. ANGELA POLISTENA, who married him, is not -- under either name. Her brother ANTONINO POLISTENA, who came on the Surriento in June 1949, is not. DOMENICA PROSTAMO is not. Enrolment required British subject status, so the clean reading is that SEBASTIANO WAS NATURALISED EARLY AND THE OTHERS WERE NOT YET. IT IS NOT PROVED, because 1959 is the last Queensland year in this collection and a naturalisation in 1960 or 1964 would be invisible here whatever happened. THE ABSENCES ARE BOUNDED BY THE COLLECTION AND NOT BY THEIR LIVES, and that sentence is the whole value of this row.

what: MELLUSO and ANILE — nothing for either in Australia
result: «Melluso» returns ZERO across all of Australia. «Anile» returns TWO, both in WESTERN AUSTRALIA on the 1949 roll: Concetta Anile and Rosario Anile.

MARIA ROSA MELLUSO is Domenica Prostamo's mother and DOMENICA ANILE is of the Briatico line; this family settled in BRISBANE, and the only Anile in the collection are two people in Western Australia, four thousand kilometres away, whose 1949 enrolment means they were naturalised long before this family landed. RECORDED TO CLOSE THEM OFF. Neither is a lead.

what: TWO SURNAME CLUSTERS IN QUEENSLAND THAT THIS ARCHIVE HAS NOT OPENED — Donato and Nicotra
result: DONATO: 65 results, with a Queensland block including CANDELORE DONATO (1941, 1949), CANDO DONATO (1939, 1959), DOMENICO DONATO (1959), ANNUNZIATO, CONCETTA and DOMINICO. NICOTRA: 39 results, almost all Queensland — FILIPPO (1934-1959), GREGORIO (1939-1959), GIUSEPPE, CARMELA, LEONARDA and LEONARD (1934-1959).
note: TWO NAMES OFF THIS FAMILY'S OWN SPINE, IN NUMBERS, IN THE RIGHT STATE, AND NOBODY HAS LOOKED. CANDELORO DONATO IS ONE OF THIS ARCHIVE'S FOUR WALLS -- born about 1783 at Scilla, the point where the Donato quarter stops -- and a CANDELORE DONATO is enrolled in Queensland in 1941 and 1949. He is obviously not the same man. THAT IS THE POINT: southern Italian families name a grandson for his grandfather, so a Candeloro Donato in Queensland is what a DESCENDANT of the wall looks like from the other side of the world. DOMENICO DONATO is the name of the man whose 1816 birth act came out of the Scilla processetti this week. NICOTRA IS SEBASTIANO MAZZA'S MOTHER'S NAME -- Maria Concetta Nicotra -- and there is a Nicotra family enrolled continuously in Queensland from 1934 to 1959. NEITHER CLUSTER IS CLAIMED HERE. A roll carries no parents and no birth year, so none of this can be attached from the rolls alone; both are written down as leads with a route, not as findings.

what: Two things that make a Findmypast sweep cheap — and one bad inference they exposed
result: javascript_tool WORKS on both the results page and the transcript page, returning every row with its /transcript?id= href in ONE page load, and the full transcript as plain text. The rolls are ordered ALPHABETICALLY BY GIVEN NAME within a surname within a sub-district.
note: THE FIRST HALVES THE COST OF EVERY FUTURE SWEEP. Clicking result rows does nothing useful -- the name is not a link and ref-clicks do not register -- and pagination has no URL form at all. But one javascript_exec over «a[href*=/transcript?id=]» returns the whole page of results with hrefs, and the same call on a transcript returns every field as text, with no screenshots and no zooming. THE SECOND KILLED AN INFERENCE I HAD ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN. Seeing Angela Mazza at 1844 and Rosario at 1845, both at 225 Leichhardt Street, I recorded that CONSECUTIVE ROLL NUMBERS MEAN ONE ADDRESS. The Crupi disprove it flatly: 504 Antonio at DEAN STREET, 505 Francesco at INNISFAIL ROAD, 510 Pietro at BIRKALA -- consecutive, three addresses, and the sequence is simply Antonio, Francesco, Giovanna, Maria, Mario, Nellie, Pietro in alphabetical order. THE ADDRESS IS THE EVIDENCE OF A HOUSEHOLD; THE NUMBERING IS EVIDENCE OF NOTHING. The Leichhardt Street row has been corrected in place.

what: THE UGOLINO VIVALDI CANDIDATE CANNOT BE UPGRADED HERE — Findmypast is holding the same record
result: «Domenico Mazza», 1951, arrival 01 MAR 1951, ship UGOLINO VIVALDI, Genoa to Australia, BARCODE 30133197 — the identical NAA barcode this archive already carries. No age, no sex, no birth year, no other field the index did not already give.
note: ROW 100 ASKED WHETHER THE SUBSCRIPTION COULD SETTLE DOMENICA PROSTAMO'S CROSSING. IT CANNOT, AND THE BARCODE IS THE PROOF. The archive graded this crossing «candidate» on a careful argument: right month, right year, right port of embarkation, right MARRIED surname, and a given name one letter out -- «Domenico» for Domenica. WHAT WOULD LIFT IT TO DOCUMENTED IS AN AGE OR A SEX, and this transcript has neither, because it is not a second witness. It is the SAME NAA INDEX ENTRY, item 30133197, re-served under a Findmypast id. THE CANDIDATE GRADE STANDS UNCHANGED. THE ROUTE THAT WOULD SETTLE IT IS FREE AND IS NOT THIS ONE: the transcript links straight to the NAA's own image viewer for barcode 30133197, and the ORIGINAL HANDWRITTEN MANIFEST would show the age, the sex, and everyone else travelling on that page -- including, if the family account is right, a two-year-old Salvatore.

what: For twentieth-century Australian arrivals, Findmypast IS the NAA index — not a second source
result: Every post-1945 row in «Australia, Inward, Outward & Coastal Passenger Lists 1826-1972» carries an id of the form ANZ/AUSPASS/NAA/xxxxxxxxx, a NAA BARCODE, and a link to recordsearch.naa.gov.au. The pre-1940 rows are different material — ANZ/VCPL and ANZ/MIGR/VICTORIAPASSLIST, the Victorian inward, outward and coastal lists.
note: THIS DEFLATES ROW 100 THE WAY THE COVERAGE FINDING DEFLATED ROW 99. The row hoped a full subscription would let the nine unnamed crossings be swept properly and the Ugolino Vivaldi candidate tested. BUT THE AUSTRALIAN ARRIVALS HERE ARE THE NAA PASSENGER INDEX, WHICH THIS ARCHIVE HAS ALREADY WORKED DIRECTLY AND FOR NOTHING. A name absent from the NAA index is absent from Findmypast, and a name present carries the same fields. THE SUBSCRIPTION ADDS TWO THINGS AND ONLY TWO: a far better SEARCH over that index -- wildcards, given-name matching and a real year filter, none of which the NAA's own interface does well -- and the VICTORIAN LISTS, which are genuinely not in the NAA index and which cover 1852-1923. THE VICTORIAN LISTS ARE THE PART WORTH MINING and no row has ever asked for them.

what: ROCCO PROSTAMO, 10 August 1949 — a Prostamo crossing this archive has never held
result: Mr Rocco Prostamo, arrival 10 AUG 1949, ship NAPOLI, Genoa to MELBOURNE, Victoria. NAA barcode 9245827.
note: A SIXTH PROSTAMO IN THE INDEX, AND THE FIRST NOBODY HERE HAS SEEN. The archive holds five -- Domenica (candidate, 1951), Domenico F (1956), Francesca and Francesco (1957), Caterina (1969) -- and this one is new. HE LANDS IN AUGUST 1949, TWO MONTHS BEFORE SEBASTIANO MAZZA came in on the Toscana and two months after the Polistena came in on the Surriento. HE IS NOT IN THE TREE. Domenica Prostamo's brothers are Domenico, Antonio Giacomo and Alfonso; her father was Francesco. NO ROCCO. what: The year filter on Findmypast is «eventyear», and «year» is one of the parameters that lies
result: «year=1898» returns ZERO on a search whose unfiltered form plainly contains 1898 rows. «eventyear=1898» returns TWELVE. The sort keys, read out of the page's own column headers, are firstname, lastname, yearofbirth, EVENTYEAR, departureport and destinationport.
note: CAUGHT BY THE RULE WRITTEN EARLIER THE SAME DAY, AND IT WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE PRODUCED A PUBLISHED FALSEHOOD. The first search run against this collection was «lastname=mazza&year=1951», which returned «No results found» -- and the conclusion sitting ready to be written was that NO MAZZA ARRIVED IN AUSTRALIA IN 1951. The control test on a year known to hold rows showed the parameter itself was dead. THE SORT KEYS ARE WORTH KEEPING because they are also the filter names, and they can be read straight off the page rather than guessed.

what: ROCCO ARENA ENTERS THE AMERICAN CENSUS ONCE, IN 1900, AND NEVER APPEARS AGAIN
result: 1900: EXACTLY ONE Rocco Arena in the whole United States — born 1861, Italy, New York — and he is ours. 1910: ZERO. 1920: two, born 1883 and 1913. 1930: six, the earliest born 1882. None of the later ones can be him.
note: THIS TURNS A GAP INTO A FINDING, AND THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES IT ONE. The archive already knew Rocco Arena was missing from the 1910 census where it expected him. THAT IS A WEAKER STATEMENT THAN IT SOUNDS -- a man can be missed, misspelt, or enumerated in the wrong ward. What is checked here is the whole country: 543 ARENA households are indexed in the 1910 census and NOT ONE HOLDS A ROCCO. Nor a GENEROSA, nor a SERAFINA, nor a CLEMENTINA. AND THE SAME SEARCH FINDS HIM IN 1900 ON THE FIRST TRY, one hit, right birth year, right state -- so the instrument works and the absence is real. THREE INDEPENDENT ABSENCES NOW POINT THE SAME WAY, and they were found by three different routes: no census entry after 1900, no Generosa on the 1913 manifest he sailed on, and no New York draft registration for the son born in Manhattan in 1896. THE HOUSEHOLD WENT HOME TO SCILLA, and the boy born on Mulberry Street was living in Italy when America called up his year.

what: The naturalisation is still not found, and the census now says where to look for it
result: No Rocco Arena in the United States Naturalization Petitions set on Findmypast; that collection begins too late for him. Nothing in the censuses of 1910, 1920 or 1930.
note: HE SAILED AS A US CITIZEN IN 1913, SO THE PAPERS EXIST. WHAT IS NEW IS THE DATE THEY MUST FALL BETWEEN. He is in America from 1892, he is in the 1900 census, and he is gone from the country by 1910 -- so HIS DECLARATION AND PETITION WERE FILED IN NEW YORK BETWEEN 1892 AND ROUGHLY 1906. THAT IS BEFORE THE FEDERAL SYSTEM WAS STANDARDISED in 1906, which is precisely why the Findmypast collection cannot see him: it begins after the period in which he must have filed. PRE-1906 NATURALISATIONS WERE HEARD IN STATE, COUNTY AND CITY COURTS as well as federal ones, and for New York City they are covered by a NARA index to petitions filed in New York courts, 1792-1906, on microfilm and not on any subscription site. NO SUBSCRIPTION WILL FIND THIS MAN. It is the National Archives at New York City, and the search is now bounded to a fourteen-year window instead of a lifetime.
